qa_pairs.question: What was the issue with ISO C++ standards regarding concurrency and memory models prior to 2011?
qa_pairs.answer: Prior to 2011, the ISO C++ standards did not include definitions for concurrency and memory models. This meant that code compiled before C++11 offered no guarantees concerning the ordering of memory reads and writes under concurrency, which was likely undefined behaviour.

qa_pairs.question: Why is it recommended to compile concurrent C++ code using C++11 or newer standards?
qa_pairs.answer: It is preferable to compile concurrent C++ code as C++11 code (or newer) because earlier ISO C++ standards (prior to 2011) lacked definitions for concurrency and memory models. This absence meant there were no guarantees about the ordering of memory reads and writes, potentially resulting in undefined behaviour.
